summary: Microburst metering lag causing invoice smoothing discrepancy
description: Issue summary: Customer reports a $3,820 negative adjustment on invoice #INV-2026-03-08 after a scheduled smoothing job; LexiTech observed credits applied then revoked the next hour. Impact: Billing inaccuracy and customer concern; affecting monthly close for LexiTech (enterprise) and blocking finance reconciliation. Environment: prod (us-west primary, with replica in eu-west). Timeline: bursts of high embedding traffic (microbursts) on 2026-03-07 23:40-23:47 UTC; billing smoothing job ran at 2026-03-08 00:00 UTC. Observed symptom: provisional credits created then dropped when smoothing completed, resulting in final invoice delta. Customer-facing impact: incorrect invoice line and confusion; customer requests reversal and justification for adjustments.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Recreate microburst: send ~1.2M embedding tokens over 8 minutes from a single org key
2) Confirm ingestion postbacks arrive with intermittent latencies (multiple >10s)
3) Wait for hourly billing smoothing job to execute and observe provisional credit creation and subsequent cleanup
4) Check invoice generation for smoothing adjustments applied to hourly line items

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: delayed ingestion postbacks (latency spikes) caused events to be split across smoothing windows. The smoothing algorithm merges events within a 1h window and applies provisional credits; delayed replays triggered a re-evaluation that removed the provisional credit. Possible causes identified: (a) debatching behavior in ingestion-service during microbursts that batches postbacks into fewer larger events, (b) billing-smoother treated reprocessed postbacks as duplicates and cancelled provisional credits, (c) race between provisional credit commit and delayed postback merge. Observed that postback latency spike (~1.2s and one >1s) correlates with larger-than-expected payloads. SRE Marta Lopez confirmed smoothing job re-eval path executed at 00:00:40 and marked final_commit=true only after reversal. No sign of double-billing, but timing race produced temporary provisional credit then reversal. Investigative actions taken: pulled raw postback queue, examined reprocessing logs, replayed smoothing job in staging with microburst fixture. Unit test coverage gap found in smoothing logic for events with out-of-order timestamps.
resolution: Workaround provided: issued provisional invoice credit of $3,820 to LexiTech and created a temporary audit note on invoice #INV-2026-03-08 to explain adjustment. Short-term fix: disable automatic provisional reversal path for smoothing jobs while we patch. Long-term fix: update billing-smoother to add microburst-exemption heuristics and strengthen duplicate-detection by transaction_id and event_fingerprint; reduce re-eval window from 60s to 10s for late postbacks with an explicit 'late' flag. Patch PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-metering/pull/934. Rollout plan: canary patch to staging on 2026-03-14, prod rollout 2026-03-17 after verification. Follow-up: add automated test and a dashboard alert when smoothing runs reverse provisional credits more than twice in an hour.
